title: Merge-interruption scratchpad: resuming context and safe merge checklist
body:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for safely resuming interrupted PR reviews and merges. I wanted a compact, repeatable checklist to reduce mistakes when context switching (e.g., I reviewed half the diff, got pulled into an incident, now must finish and merge).

TL;DR: short checklist at the top, deeper heuristics and follow-ups below. Use this when you return to a PR after any >= 30m interruption.

Quick checklist (run through out loud if nervous):
- Re-read PR description and the linked ticket quick summary (1–2 mins).
- Check CI status (unit / integration / e2e / linters) and recent rerun timestamps.
- Confirm target branch is still correct and up-to-date with main (rebase/merge needed?).
- Scan changed files list for unexpected churn (new dependencies, formatting in many files, generated code).
- Verify test coverage touched by change: are there new tests? failing flakes?
- Confirm deploy gating: does this touch runtime, infra, migrations, or public API? If yes, get a second reviewer and slower rollout.
- Smoke-run one manual happy-path locally (fast command below).
- If all good, merge with message noting who approved and any post-merge follow-ups.

Heuristics / why each item matters:
- PR description: authors sometimes update later; if outdated, call out before merging.
- CI timestamps: green 12h ago + new commits -> re-run; green 5m ago but unrelated flaky tests -> investigate flakiness marker.
- Target branch drift: small drift is fine if CI covers it; larger drift (>= 50 commits or many conflicting areas) -> require rebase and quick smoke.
- Unexpected churn: mass reformatting or large autogenerated files should be handled in separate PRs. If present, ask for author to split or explain.
- Tests: no test additions for behavior change -> ask for minimal assertion; if adding tests, check they exercise the new logic, not only helpers.

Quick local smoke commands (serving-runtime):
- ./dev/run_local.sh --service serving --fast
- curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":4}' | jq .
- pytest tests/unit/test_batching.py::test_small_batch -q
- watch logs: tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/serving.log | grep -i "error\|warn"

Merge safety gates (if any of these true, hold and ask for more review):
- touches: authentication, billing, data plane, migration scripts, model weights loading path, public API signature, or rollout config defaults.
- introduces or relaxes a feature flag without documented rollback plan.
- changes concurrency/batching defaults that could affect latency/cost (ping SRE).
- adds new native dependency (C/C++ lib) or a new systemd service.

Rollback / quick mitigation plan (write this into the PR when merging if risky):
- revert PR + re-deploy previous tag (ops playbook link: ENG-ops/deploy-rollback.md).
- enable safe fallback: set ROUTING_POLICY=legacy in console (if feature toggled).
- short-circuit: hotfix that reverts config change only (less invasive).

Small follow-ups to add to PR description if merging: (copy into the PR checklist)
- [ ] Add a note to changelog (internal) with risk level and test coverage summary.
- [ ] Add a one-line troubleshooting note for oncall (if affects runtime).
- [ ] Create a short perf smoke ticket to run 1h of synthetic traffic if change touches batching.

Observability / monitoring to watch for after merge (timeline + metrics):
- 0–15m: error rate, 95th latency, token/sec, worker OOMs (alert thresholds lowered for 30m).
- 15–60m: slow error trends, tail latency shifts, CPU/GPU utilization.
- 24h: cost delta / token-unit cost (if any config changed).

Notes-to-self: common mistakes I make when resuming:
- I forget that the author renamed a helper and kept reading old variable names in my head -> always open the diff with word-wrap off so renames jump out.
- I assume CI passing once but forget to re-run after rebase.
- I skim tests but miss an assertion that only checks internal helper behavior.
- I approve refactors with implicit behavioral changes (pay extra attention to conditional branching and defaults).

Refactor follow-up ideas (grab one and make a small ticket):
- Break out large PRs that change both API surface and implementation into two: API contract (with compatibility tests) + impl refactor.
- Add a tiny test harness to allow deterministic local runs for the hot path we touched (example: a lightweight batch simulator).
- Add a lint rule or github action to fail PRs that touch both /pkg/api and /pkg/infra in the same commit without a review tag.

Unresolved questions to ask author before merging (copy into review comment if not answered):
- Why was the default value changed from X to Y? Is there a migration concern for existing deployments?
- Did you consider the scenario where cache key includes request.metadata.user_agent? Could be noisy.
- Are there any backwards-incompatible serialization changes? If so, tag for a slow rollout.

Quick template for post-merge comment (paste into PR):
"Merged at TIMESTAMP after green CI and manual smoke. Post-merge watch list: error rate + 95p latency for 1h (lower thresholds). Follow-ups: ENG-XXXX (perf smoke), ENG-YYYY (changelog + oncall note). If you see a regression, revert PR and run rollback playbook. — Adele"

Mental model heuristics (fast):
- If the change is > 200 LOC and touches runtime path, treat as medium risk.
- If it touches public API or data format, treat as high risk.
- If only refactor tests or non-runtime docs, low risk.

Stickers / micro-checks (tiny things I often miss):
- Did you update feature-flag default README?
- Any TODOs left in code? (search TODO("revisit") etc)
- Did formatters re-write unrelated files? (check repo root .gitattributes/.prettier config)
- Is there a migration file missing from change list?

Next actions (if I'm the reviewer finishing this):
- If low risk: re-run CI, run smoke commands, merge with squash, and paste the post-merge comment.
- If medium risk: request one more approver (SRE or owner), schedule canary deploy for 30 mins, then full rollout.
- If high risk: request feature-flag gating, add a rollout plan, and pair with author for merge.

Random scratch ideas (useful later):
- Could we add an "interrupt-resume" label that auto-inserts a small checklist into the PR UI for reviewers who mark themselves as "stepping away"?
- Small bot: if reviewer comments with "paused" and returns later, bot could run a diff of reviewer view vs current head and highlight changed files since pause.

Footer: this is intentionally terse and messy — it's a working habit doc. If it becomes useful more broadly, we can promote to an eng playbook page and add automations.

-- Adele
